m01-proof.label: Does this comparison against position 3 prove strict dominance?

options.a: Yes: it is enough for 2 to beat 1 against one possible choice by the opponent.
options.b: No: strict dominance requires comparing 1 and 2 against every possible choice by the opponent.
options.c: No: dominance requires both candidates to receive more votes.

m02-round.label: The result of the second round

options.a: Positions 3 and 4 remain; all 60 voters still vote.
options.b: Positions 3 and 4 remain; only the 20 voters in the central groups still vote.
options.c: Positions 2, 3, 4, 5 remain: no further strict dominance is possible.
options.d: Only 3 remains: a rational candidate must choose one particular central position.

m03-shares.label: Your vote share at position 2 and at position 3

options.b: 3 does not strictly dominate 2: this is a counterexample. Dominance in the other direction has not been established.
options.c: No dominance claim can be disproved until every strategy profile has been checked.

m05-dominance.label: Does C strictly dominate A and B?

options.a: Yes: C has the highest expected payoff when L and R are equally likely.
options.b: We cannot check because the opponent's payoffs are unknown.
options.c: No: C does worse than A against L and worse than B against R.
